newsitem.title: INDIA: One in three India phones seen eventually wireless.
newsitem.headline: One in three India phones seen eventually wireless.

text.p: One in three fixed line phones installed in India over the next five years will be wireless, a senior telecommunications official said on Friday.

"We expect 30 percent of all phones installed over the next five years to be wireless phones," Telecommunications Commission member N.K. Sinha told a Universal Wireless Communications Consortium conference.
The Telecommunications Commission is the highest government body and oversees the Department of Telecommunications (DoT).
Wireless technology uses radio waves instead of wires to connect ordinary telephones.
Sinha said the Commission was looking into what band widths were available for wireless fixed line phones, and was working on finding ways for the optimal use of band widths.
He said wireless telephony held the key to the spread of the information superhighway in India as existing copper cables in the ground do not have the capacity to deal with the demand.
"Wireless broadband networks are around the corner, and this will cater to the demand of delivering voice, video and data over a single telephone line," Sinha said.
DoT has already set in motion plans to add wireless phones. It recently tendered for 30,000 wireless phones in central India, and is finalising another for 60,000 wireless phones in 11 cities.
It has also tested a 1,000-line wireless phone pilot in Delhi and will soon be offering these to subscribers.
The other big push for wireless phones will come from India's private fixed line operators, who won licences in a 1995 auction. Each of them are required to install wireless phones in urban areas.
India's installed phone base is 13 million phones. Over the next three years, DoT estimates the number will cross 20 million, split between itself and private operators.
On Thursday, Hughes Network Systems Inc, (HNS) said it expects the wireless phone market in India to be worth $1 billion over the next three years.
HNS is a unit of Hughes Electronics Corp, which is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp.
